title: 1.1 My best friend
text:

# What is a good friend like?
- My best friend is funny and kind.
- She is always helpful.
- He is sporty and very clever.
# Describe your friend
[satz: Amira | *is* | my best friend.]
[satz: She | *has got* | long black hair.]
[satz: We | *like* | the same music.]

| long hair, curly hair | helpful, chatty | listens to music |

Richtig: She has got brown eyes.
# Das Adjektiv
Falsch: She has got hair long.
Richtig: She has got long hair.
Achtung: Das Adjektiv steht vor dem Nomen. Das ist wie im Deutschen.

title: 1.2 That's mine! Possessive pronouns
text:
# Whose is it?
[dialog: Teacher Whose bag is this? | Ben It's not mine. Maybe it's Amira's. | Amira Yes, it's mine! Thank you. | Teacher And whose phone is this? | Ben That's mine.]
# my bag – mine
Vor einem Nomen: my, your … Ohne Nomen: mine, yours …
| vor dem Nomen | ohne Nomen |
|---|---|
| It's my bag. | It's mine. |
| It's your bag. | It's yours. |
| It's his bag. | It's his. |
| It's her bag. | It's hers. |
| It's our bag. | It's ours. |
| It's their bag. | It's theirs. |
# Sentence blocks
[satz: This | *is* | my cap.]
[satz: This cap | *is* | mine.]
[satz: The ball | *is* | theirs.]
Merke: Frage mit Whose …? (Wem gehört …?) Antwort mit mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.
help:
# Kein Nomen nach mine
Falsch: It's mine bag.
Richtig: It's my bag. Oder: It's mine.
# Kein Apostroph
Falsch: The pen is your's.
Richtig: The pen is yours.
Falsch: The house is their's.
Richtig: The house is theirs.
Achtung: yours, hers, ours, theirs schreibst du ohne Apostroph.
# Whose oder Who's
Falsch: Who's bag is this?
Richtig: Whose bag is this?
Achtung: Who's = who is. Whose = wem gehört.

title: 1.4 Myself, yourself: Reflexive pronouns
text:
# I can do it myself!
| Person | reflexiv | Beispiel |

| she | herself | She hurt herself. |
| it | itself | The cat washes itself. |

title: 2.1 Welcome to Bavaria
text:
# My home region
- I live in Bavaria. Bavaria is in the south of Germany.
- The capital of Bavaria is Munich.
- The highest mountain in Germany is the Zugspitze.
# In my town
[satz: There | *is* | a big park | in my town.]
[satz: There | *are* | two cinemas | in Augsburg.]
[satz: There | *isn't* | a zoo | in our village.]

title: 2.4 Word order: place before time
text:
# The English sentence
Im englischen Satz gilt: Subjekt – Verb – Objekt. Dann kommt zuerst der Ort, dann die Zeit.
[satz: I | *play* | football | in the park | on Saturdays.]
[satz: We | *meet* | our friends | at the café | after school.]
[satz: Lena | *went* | to Munich | yesterday.]
# Ort vor Zeit
| Wer? | Verb | Was? | Wo? | Wann? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| I | play | football | in the park | on Saturdays. |
| Ali | buys | bread | at the bakery | every morning. |
| We | watched | a film | at the cinema | last Friday. |
[uhr: 8:00=at school at eight | 16:30=at the pool at half past four]
# Deutsch und Englisch
- Deutsch: Am Samstag spiele ich im Park Fußball.
- Englisch: I play football in the park on Saturdays.
Merke: Merk dir P vor T – Place before Time. Wie im Alphabet: P kommt vor T.
help:
# Verb an zweiter Stelle
Falsch: On Saturday play I football.
Richtig: I play football on Saturday.
Achtung: Im Englischen steht das Subjekt immer direkt vor dem Verb.

Falsch: I play in the park football.
Richtig: I play football in the park.
# Ort vor Zeit
Falsch: We meet after school at the café.
Richtig: We meet at the café after school.
Achtung: Die Zeit darf auch ganz am Anfang stehen: After school, we meet at the café.

title: 8.4 Linking sentences: so and when
text:
# so: deshalb
Mit so sagst du, was dann passiert. Zuerst der Grund, dann die Folge.
[satz: It | *was* | sunny, | so | we | *went* | to the lake.]
[satz: I | *was* | hungry, | so | I | *made* | a sandwich.]
# when: wenn, als
Mit when sagst du, wann etwas passiert.
[satz: When | it | *rains*, | I | *watch* | a film.]
[satz: I | *watch* | a film | when | it | *rains*.]
| Wort | Bedeutung | Beispiel |
|---|---|---|
| so | deshalb, also | It was late, so I took a taxi. |
| when | wenn, als | When I'm bored, I read comics. |
| and | und | I play football and I swim. |
| but | aber | I like pizza, but I don't like fish. |
| because | weil | I'm happy because it's Friday. |
[dialog: Leni What did you do in the holidays? | Arjun It rained a lot, so we went to the cinema. | Leni And when the weather was good? | Arjun When it was sunny, we went cycling in the mountains. | Leni Sounds great!]
[uhr: 15:00=When the sun shines, I go out. | 20:00=When it's dark, I go home.]
Merke: Vor so steht ein Komma. Steht when am Anfang, steht ein Komma in der Mitte.
help:
# so und because
Falsch: I was tired, so I went to bed because.
Richtig: I was tired, so I went to bed. Oder: I went to bed because I was tired.
Achtung: so = Folge (deshalb). because = Grund (weil).
# Wortstellung nach so
Falsch: It was cold, so wore I a jacket.
Richtig: It was cold, so I wore a jacket.
Achtung: Nach so bleibt die Reihenfolge: Subjekt – Verb.
# when
Achtung: when = immer wenn oder als. Im Deutschen „wenn“ und „als“ – im Englischen oft beides when.
